institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ranking of the university and the courses offered as well as the academic and intellectual level of the institution

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience at the receiving institution and would consider it for a graduate degree. I also had a great experience in the host city and the culture. I lacked a little in the social life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, especially because I participated in the introductory week offered by the receiving institution.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No direct assistance but I participated in the introductory week before classes which was a great start and a great help with a lot of useful information to get me started on my exchange

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky in finding a flat that I would afford but I fear that it would have been really difficult to find suitable and affordable housing off campus if I did not get lucky early on in the process

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive and difficult to find good housing in Paris

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know what housing was available to students

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a "first come, first serve" process online so you had to prepare your course list and your back-up courses (in case you did not get your preferential courses) ahead. Then it was very important to be ready on the dot when registration opened and be very quick because many courses became unavailable fast. Ahead of it, it was daunting to know I had to be so quick on an interface I had never used before. While using it, however, it was easy enough. This was especially because I had watched the instruction videos and participated in a webinar about course registration provided by the receiving institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Instruction videos and an interactive webinar about course registration provided by the receiving institution

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get all the classes I wanted because I had prepared a lot ahead of time so I could complete my registration in less than two minutes after it opened

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare ahead of time and be ready on the dot! Also register to courses in priority so you register for the most important courses first and especially those you know will have limited spaces (e.g. lecture courses often allow for many more students and will thus not be filled up as quickly as other types)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great variety of classes offered in English to exchange students

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were all 2nd year BA courses as Sciences Po only offer this level to exchange students due to the structure of their BA-degrees

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Each classes had more deliverables during the semester than I was used to at UCPH. They also had a syllabus that was a lot shorter than I was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Politics, European integration and its challenges:
the euro, migration and populism, Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider's view (The), (Un)Making The World: Critical Approaches To International Law, The Politics And Strategy Of UNPK

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider's view (The), (Un)Making The World: Critical Approaches To International Law, The Politics And Strategy Of UNPK

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs. The introductory week cost €200 to be paid by the student if they wish to participate

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected - especially vegetables

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different athletic and cultural activities to register for at the beginning of the semester and then being held over the following 12 weeks. Also a lot of student organizations on campus

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did Krav Maga and a painting class. I would definitely recommend Krav Maga! The painting class was too short to really benefit from.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the museums of Paris - many of the are free for EU citizens under 25 years. Also visit the smaller cafés and brasseries in the different neighborhoods - find the hidden gems

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as it is not very different from my home culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Set in early and participate in social activities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social activities surrounding dining out and drinking coffee / wine during the week and week-end

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a different but equal academic burden which demands time and effort. Participate early in the social activities because it can be hard to make friends. Spend your days exploring the city and take advantage of living in Paris!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Paris and my academic successes at such a recognized institution. It was also great to experience a different academic culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
